summary:
## Version caveat (important)

arXiv:2511.08436 has **two very different versions**. **v1 (11 Nov 2025)** is a ~1,800-word workshop abstract (NeurIPS 2025 "AI for non-human animal communication" workshop) with essentially no quantitative methods. **v2 (19 Jul 2026)** is the full paper (~13k words + 10 supplementary sections) and is the only source of technical detail. All numbers below are from v2 unless flagged. Code: `https://github.com/KempnerInstitute/wef`. Local extracted full text at `<local-scratch> (and `fish_v1.txt`).

## 1. EOD / electric-field physics

Electrostatic, quasi-static, 2D. Two source classes: (a) actively controlled **monopole pairs** modeling pulsatile EODs — two internal monopoles ±q at ±d/4 along the body axis (separation 1.0 cm, q_EOD = ±1.11×10⁻¹⁵ C); (b) **always-on intrinsic dipoles** on agents (p = (1.11×10⁻²³, 0) C·m) and prey (p = (0, 1.11×10⁻²⁴) C·m).

- E_active(r) = (1/4πε₀) Σᵢ qᵢ(r−rᵢ)/|r−rᵢ|³  (Eq. 1) — monopole, **1/r² decay**
- E_intrinsic(r) = (1/4πε₀) Σᵢ [3(pᵢ·r̂ᵢ)r̂ᵢ − pᵢ]/|r−rᵢ|³  (Eq. 2) — dipole, **1/r³ decay**
- Induced dipole on conducting spheres: p_induced = 4πε₀R³χ E_external (Eq. 3), χ = (ε/ε₀−1)/(ε/ε₀+2) = **−0.5** (Chen et al. 2005)
- Walls: **method of images**, non-conducting, first-order only (single reflection, no sign flip), image scale 0.95
- E_total = E_active + E_intrinsic + E_induced + E_reflected

There is **no transdermal-potential model** in the usual electrophysiological sense. Transduction is: s = E(r_s)·n, projecting the local field onto a radially outward sensor normal on a circular body. Then baseline subtraction (intrinsic + self-EOD corollary discharge always; a **dynamic cons-baseline** recomputed each timestep for cons-image extraction, following Pedraja & Sawtell 2024), then sign-preserving log-magnitude normalization to [−1,1]: m̃ = clip(|s|, E_min, E_max); m̂ = [log₁₀ max(m̃,ε) − log₁₀E_min]/[log₁₀E_max − log₁₀E_min], ŝ = sgn(s)·m̂, with ε = 10⁻²⁵.

**Receptors (72 channels total per agent in N=4):** Mormyromasts N_m = **36** (30% concentrated in the frontal 60° "chin fovea", rest uniform on the circumference); Ampullary N_a = **24** uniform; Knollenorgans N_k = **12 per conspecific** (12×3 = 36 for N=4), encoding **only the sign** of the local field plus a scalar conspecific-size metadata channel. Ranges: Mormyromast 5 cm (prey) / 10 cm (conspecific, R_M); Ampullary 4 cm / 8 cm; Knollenorgan 100 cm (R_K). Thresholds (V/m): E_A,min 2×10⁻¹⁰, E_A,max 2×10⁻⁸, E_M,min 5×10⁻⁸, E_M,max 5×10⁻², E_K,min 2×10⁻⁷, E_K,log-max 2×10⁻⁴. Cons-image scaling factor k_cons = 100.

**Noise model: there is none.** No sensory noise, receptor noise, EOD timing jitter, or channel noise anywhere in the paper. The only stochasticity is policy sampling during training (disabled at evaluation — deterministic policy mean).

## 2. Action / observation / reward

**Actions (4):** continuous forward translation, continuous angular rotation, EOD emission logit (thresholded to binary), bite logit (thresholded to binary). Speed bounds from empirical WEF tracking data, scaled by the agent's size parameter.

**Observations:** 36 Mormyromast + 24 Ampullary + (12×3 Knollenorgan + per-conspecific size scalar) + last action vector + egocentric displacement vectors + own size scalar. Fixed length for N=4; zero-padded for fewer agents.

**Reward (Eq. 4):** r_t = r_food + r_prox + r_bitten + r_bite + r_collision + r_effort, where r_food = +c_f per food item, r_prox = c_p·(d_{t−1}^food − d_t^food)/P_arena, r_bitten scaled by (1 + s_biter − s_victim), r_bite a small cost, r_collision a penalty, r_effort a penalty for movement/turn commands above threshold. **Numeric coefficient values are never given** — §5.6 says "Reward coefficient values are given in Supplementary Section .15.3" but .15.3 lists only symbols. Timestep and wall-proximity terms were zero. **No EOD emission cost, no communication or coordination reward.**

## 3. Arena / task

dt = **12 ms (83 Hz)**, chosen to match the WEF social echo response latency (Schuster 2001). N = 4 default. Training arena width and height independently sampled from [40, 300] cm per episode. Eval arenas: 70×70 cm (four-agent patchy, homing, two-agent square), 160×40 cm (two-agent wide), 150×150 cm (dyadic one-patch), 40×40 cm (collective-sensing ablation). Agent radius 1 cm, prey radius 0.25 cm. Food: Poisson draw at density ρ₀, **no replenishment or decay** except the dyadic central patch which replenishes continuously. Four distributions: uniform, patchy (4 patches × 5 cm radius × 40 items), N-patch (N ∈ {1..5} on an ellipse), one-patch. **Episode length in steps/seconds is never stated** (the dyadic assay implies 10 s acclimation + 40 s foraging).

## 4. Training

**MAPPO** (Yu et al. 2022) — recurrent, shared-parameter, CTDE (centralized critic sees all agents' concatenated observations; decentralized execution, Dec-POMDP, no explicit communication channel). GAE λ = 0.95, PPO clip ε = 0.2, truncated BPTT. **20 seeds × 5M environment steps each**, ~6–9 h/seed on one RTX 5090. Architecture: separate actor and critic, each = 2-layer MLP encoder (ReLU + LayerNorm, 512) → single-layer **GRU with D_H = 512** → linear head; action head emits continuous movement + EOD logit + bite logit. (Note: §5.6 says "tanh" while .15.4 says "ReLU + LayerNorm" — an internal inconsistency; v1 said all layers tanh.) **Hyperparameters were taken unchanged from the MAPPO codebase with no tuning; no learning rate, batch size, discount factor, or entropy coefficient values are reported.** Seed selection was ethological, not reward-based: filter seeds with non-positive intercept in food_eaten_i = β₀ + β₁·size_i, then rank by total food, median slope β₁, median R². Seed **S1** used for all analyses. The authors concede this makes Fig. 3M (larger agents eat more) "a quantitative confirmation, not an independent finding."

## 5. Interventions

(a) **Sensor ablations** — zero the input channels for each receptor class at eval time, no retraining; plus mixed two-sensor, Knollenorgan-only, all-off controls; run in 70×70 cm patchy arenas plus a solo-agent control to separate individual from social effects. (b) **Collective-sensing ablations** — within Mormyromasts, gate self-image vs cons-image independently (control / self-EOD-only / cons-EOD-only), in a 40×40 cm arena, 30 runs each. (c) **EOD muting** — "one of the four agents had its EOD emission silenced for the duration of the evaluation; all other policy components remained intact, so the muted agent could still sense and move but emitted no EODs, and its conspecifics received no EOD-related input from it." Measured: total food consumed and mean nearest-neighbor distance. (d) **Food distribution** — patchy vs uniform; patch-count sweep 1–5 under iso-food and unconstrained; scarcity multipliers 0.5× and 0.25×. (e) **Bot control** — resident replaced by a patch-confined random walker, frozen vs moving × stochastic EOD rate including zero (300-condition grid).

## 6. "Communication" — operational definition and the gap

Their definition, verbatim (Intro): *"Here, we use 'communication' to refer operationally to EOD signals that are sensed by conspecifics via Knollenorgans and that influence their behavior."* This is **purely effect-based**: it requires only that a receiver detect the EOD and change behavior. It does **not** require sender benefit, does not distinguish **cue from signal**, and does not require that the emission be produced *because* it influences receivers.

Evidence offered for social use: Knollenorgan ablation increases EOD probability, increases biting, and decreases spacing while leaving food intake intact; EOD muting reduces group food and increases spacing; bot patch-reach rate is higher when the bot emits than when silent, peaking at intermediate rates; EOD rate is modulated by distance to conspecific and by eating/biting/being-bitten events; Knollenorgan ablation abolishes group-size scaling of RNN effective dimensionality; PLSC shared dimensions collapse beyond 100 cm.

**What they do not and cannot distinguish** — never stated as a limitation, which is the opening: the EOD-muting manipulation is **confounded**. Because the Mormyromast self-image is defined as the distortion of *the agent's own* EOD, silencing an agent's EOD simultaneously destroys (i) its private active electrolocation and (ii) its public social signal. The reduced foraging and increased spacing therefore cannot be attributed to loss of communication rather than loss of self-generated active sensing. (An earlier WebFetch summary asserted the paper claims this "isolated the consequences of losing outgoing communication independent of impaired sensing" — that phrase does **not** appear in the paper; it was a summarizer hallucination.) More fundamentally, with **zero cost on EOD emission** and no evolutionary/selection dynamics, nothing in the model can separate signalling from incidental information leakage: an agent emits freely, so any receiver effect is a byproduct, and the framework has no way to ask whether EOD production is *maintained* by its effect on receivers.

## 7. Metabolic cost, predation, evolution — ABSENT

- **EOD metabolic/energetic cost: entirely absent.** No energy term in the reward; the only effort penalty is on movement/turn magnitude. No energetics citation in the bibliography (no Salazar & Stoddard, no Markham, no Lewis).
- **Predation: absent from the body.** Stoddard, Tran & Krahe (2019) "Predation and Crypsis in the Evolution of Electric Signaling" is ref 64 but is cited **once, in the supplementary Related Work**, and miscited — grouped under "EOD patterns carry information about identity, dominance, and aggression," not for predation risk. v1 listed predators as future work ("richer ecological contexts (e.g., predators, sex differences)"); v2 dropped predators from Limitations entirely and kept only sex differences.
- **Evolution: absent.** "Fitness" appears only as "individual fitness incentives," meaning the RL reward. v1's abstract said "evolution-inspired rewards for individual fitness"; v2 removed that framing. No selection, no heritability, no population dynamics, no phase diagram over cost/benefit.
- The single mention of cost is receiver-side: "individuals can exploit conspecific signals as public information **at low cost**" (producer-scrounger, ref 47).

## 8. Quantitative results

The paper is **strikingly number-poor** — nearly all results are reported as directional/graphical with mean ± SEM and star annotations, no effect sizes, no exact p-values in text. The only hard numbers: D_eff = **81.3** (participation ratio) with **304 PCs for 90% variance** vs D_H = 512; biting peaks at ~**40%** of normalized interaction duration; confronting interactions have the highest biting rate ≈**50%**; IDI power-law fits over **8–100 ms** by MLE with KS goodness-of-fit — and the authors explicitly state the exponents for real fish and agents **"do not quantitatively match"** (no exponent values given). Everything else (ablation effects, muting effects, patch sweeps, decoding R², PLSC r) is qualitative. Statistics: Dunnett one-vs-control for ablations, two-sided Mann-Whitney unpaired, Wilcoxon signed-rank paired, α = 0.05, **no multiple-comparison correction** ("panel-level exploratory summaries"). Decoding used OLS with grouped CV and mean-baseline-normalized R² (Methods §5.10.3), not ridge α=0.01.

Behavioral validation: curvilinear homing with bimodal error-angle distribution (parallel/anti-parallel to field lines) vs straight-line ray-casting baseline; Θ^K_error decoded better than Θ_agent; nearest-agent distance and Knollenorgan features are the top-decoded variables; wideband RNN power lower with a conspecific nearby and higher in subordinates. Notable negative result: agents show only size-dependent EOD *reduction*, **not** the full EOD cessation that real subordinate mormyrids display (refs 43, 12) — the authors flag testing this under "stronger social pressure" as future work.
key_facts: Two versions: v1 (11 Nov 2025) is a ~1,800-word NeurIPS workshop abstract with no quantitative methods; v2 (19 Jul 2026) is the full paper. All technical detail is v2-only.
Code repository: https://github.com/KempnerInstitute/wef (Kempner Institute). Local extracted text: <local-scratch> and fish_v1.txt

Authors: Satpreet H. Singh, Sonja Johnson-Yu, Zhouyang Lu, Aaron Walsman, Federico Pedraja, Denis Turcu, Pratyusha Sharma, Naomi Saphra, Nathaniel B. Sawtell, Kanaka Rajan. Categories cs.NE, cs.AI, cs.MA, eess.SY, q-bio.NC. Contact kanaka_rajan@hms.harvard.edu
EOD field Eq.1 (monopole pair, 1/r^2): E_active(r) = (1/4*pi*eps0) * sum_i q_i (r - r_i)/|r - r_i|^3
Intrinsic dipole field Eq.2 (1/r^3): E_intrinsic(r) = (1/4*pi*eps0) * sum_i [3(p_i . rhat_i) rhat_i - p_i]/|r - r_i|^3, eps0 = 8.854e-12 F/m
Induced dipole Eq.3: p_induced = 4*pi*eps0*R^3*chi*E_external, chi = (eps/eps0 - 1)/(eps/eps0 + 2) = -0.5 (Chen et al. 2005)
E_total = E_active + E_intrinsic + E_induced + E_reflected. Walls = non-conducting, method of images, FIRST-ORDER ONLY (single reflection, no sign flip), electric wall-image scale 0.95
EOD electric organ = two monopoles +/- q at +/- d/4 along body axis; q_EOD = +/-1.11e-15 C; source separation 1.0 cm
Prey intrinsic dipole moment p_prey = (0, 1.11e-24) C.m; agent intrinsic dipole moment p_agent = (1.11e-23, 0) C.m; cons-image scaling factor k_cons = 100
Sensor transduction: s = E(r_s) . n where n is the radially outward normal on the circular body. No transdermal potential model per se.
Sensor normalization: m_tilde = clip(|s|, E_min, E_max); m_hat = [log10(max(m_tilde, eps)) - log10(E_min)]/[log10(E_max) - log10(E_min)]; s_hat = sgn(s)*m_hat in [-1,1]; eps = 1e-25

Receptor counts: N_m = 36 Mormyromasts (30% packed in frontal 60 deg 'chin fovea', remainder uniform on circumference); N_a = 24 Ampullary (uniform); N_k = 12 Knollenorgans PER CONSPECIFIC (12x3 = 36 for N=4)
Knollenorgans encode ONLY the sign of the local field plus a scalar conspecific-size metadata channel; they identify direction and size but NOT distance
Detection ranges: Mormyromast prey 5 cm, Mormyromast conspecific 10 cm (R_M); Ampullary prey 4 cm, Ampullary conspecific 8 cm; Knollenorgan conspecific 100 cm (R_K)
Sensor thresholds (V/m): E_A,min 2.0e-10, E_A,max 2.0e-8, E_M,min 5.0e-8, E_M,max 5.0e-2, E_K,min 2.0e-7, E_K,log-max 2.0e-4
Mormyromast dynamic range set to baseline*1e-6 (lower) to baseline*0.25 (upper), for both self-image and residual cons-image
Dynamic cons-baseline model: s_cons-image,k = s_total,k - s_cons-baseline,k, recomputed every timestep; inspired by Pedraja & Sawtell 2024
NO NOISE MODEL ANYWHERE: no sensory noise, receptor noise, EOD timing jitter, or channel noise. Only stochasticity is policy sampling during training; evaluation uses deterministic policy mean.

Action space (4): continuous forward translation, continuous angular rotation, EOD emission logit (thresholded binary), bite logit (thresholded binary). First-order command kinematics; speed bounds from empirical WEF tracking, scaled by size parameter.

Observation vector: 36 Mormyromast + 24 Ampullary + 12x(N_agents-1) Knollenorgan + per-conspecific size scalar + last action vector + egocentric displacement vectors + own size scalar. Zero-padded for N<4.

Reward Eq.4: r_t = r_food + r_prox + r_bitten + r_bite + r_collision + r_effort. r_food = +c_f; r_prox = c_p*(d_{t-1}^food - d_t^food)/P_arena; r_bitten scaled by (1 + s_biter - s_victim); r_effort penalizes movement/turn above threshold.
REWARD COEFFICIENT VALUES ARE NEVER GIVEN. Section 5.6 points to Supp .15.3 but .15.3 lists only symbols c_f, c_p and qualitative descriptions. Timestep and wall-proximity terms were set to zero.
NO EOD EMISSION COST in the reward. The effort penalty applies only to movement/turn commands. No reward for communication, coordination, chasing, or aggression.
Timestep dt = 12 ms (83 Hz), chosen to match the WEF social echo response latency (Schuster 2001, ref 41/57), near the minimum inter-pulse interval of the species
Agent radius R_agent = 0.01 m (1 cm); prey radius R_prey = 0.0025 m (0.25 cm)
Training arena: width and height independently sampled from [40, 300] cm per episode. Homing training arena range 75-150 cm.
Eval arenas: 70x70 cm (4-agent patchy, homing, 2-agent square); 160x40 cm (2-agent wide, agents init at (20,20) and (140,20)); 150x150 cm (dyadic one-patch); 40x40 cm (collective-sensing ablation)
Food: Poisson draw at density rho_0 (pellets/cm^2), NO replenishment or decay, except the dyadic central patch which replenishes continuously. Patchy = 4 patches of 5 cm radius, 40 items per patch.
EPISODE LENGTH IN STEPS/SECONDS IS NEVER STATED. Dyadic assay implies 10 s acclimation + 40 s foraging.
Algorithm: MAPPO (Yu et al. 2022, ref 33) - recurrent, shared-parameter, CTDE. Dec-POMDP with NO explicit communication channel; critic sees concatenated observations of all agents.
GAE lambda = 0.95; PPO clip epsilon = 0.2; truncated BPTT with fixed horizon; entropy coefficient c_H (value unstated)
20 independent seeds x 5M environment steps each; ~6-9 hours per seed on a single NVIDIA RTX 5090

Architecture: separate actor and critic. Each = 2-layer MLP encoder (ReLU + LayerNorm, hidden 512) -> single-layer GRU with D_H = 512 -> linear head. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: Methods 5.6 says all hidden layers used tanh with 256-unit heads; Supp .15.4 says ReLU + LayerNorm.
Hyperparameters taken UNCHANGED from the MAPPO codebase with no tuning. No learning rate, batch size, discount factor, or entropy coefficient values reported anywhere.

Seed selection is ethological not reward-based: filter seeds with non-positive intercept in food_eaten_i = beta_0 + beta_1*agent_size_i + eps_i, then rank by total food consumed, median slope beta_1, median R^2. Seed S1 selected. Authors concede Fig 3M is 'a quantitative confirmation, not an independent finding.'

EOD muting intervention (verbatim): 'One of the four agents had its EOD emission silenced for the duration of the evaluation; all other policy components remained intact, so the muted agent could still sense and move but emitted no EODs, and its conspecifics received no EOD-related input from it.' Measured: total food consumed + mean nearest-neighbor distance.
Sensor ablations set all channels of a receptor class to zero at EVALUATION time; the policy is NOT retrained.

Collective-sensing ablation: 3 conditions (control / self-EOD-only / cons-EOD-only) within the Mormyromast channel, in a 40x40 cm arena, uniform food, 30 runs per condition. Ampullary channel unaffected.
Food-distribution interventions: patchy vs uniform; patch-count sweep N in {1,2,3,4,5} under iso-food (total fixed) and unconstrained (per-patch fixed); scarcity multipliers 0.5x and 0.25x

Bot control: resident replaced by patch-confined rule-based random walker; frozen vs moving crossed with stochastic EOD emission rate including zero; 300-condition grid over size, EOD rate, movement state, initial position

Operational definition of communication (verbatim, Introduction): 'Here, we use "communication" to refer operationally to EOD signals that are sensed by conspecifics via Knollenorgans and that influence their behavior.' Purely effect-based; no sender benefit, no cue/signal distinction.

Operational definition of emergent (verbatim): 'behaviors that were not hand-coded or directly rewarded but arose through learning under the modeled sensory, motor, ecological, and reward constraints'
D_eff = 81.3 (participation ratio, D_eff = 1/sum_i lambda_tilde_i^2); 304 PCs needed for 90% variance; D_H = 512 nominal
Biting concentrated in first half of interaction bouts, peaking at ~40% of normalized interaction duration; confronting interactions have the highest biting rate (~50%)

IDI power-law fits over 8-100 ms via MLE (Python 'powerlaw' package, Alstott et al.), KS goodness-of-fit. Authors state the exponents for real fish vs agents 'do not quantitatively match' and give NO exponent values.
Real-fish IDIs derived from Chrtkova et al. 2025 dyadic recordings at 50 kHz sampling rate; agent IDIs from the 160x40 cm two-agent wide assay, 100 episodes
Peri-event window: +/-100 timesteps (+/-1200 ms at 83 Hz), minimum 3 qualifying events per agent. EOD-rate context binning uses 15 uniform bins.

Interaction geometry thresholds: theta_close = pi/4, theta_opp = 3pi/4; contact threshold d_contact = 2 cm; reduced interaction threshold d_reduce = 5 cm. Labels: confronting, chasing, fleeing, dispersing, unaligned.

PLSC: C_XY = X^T Y, SVD, circular-shift null with n = 30 shifts, component significant only if BOTH singular value and projected correlation exceed the 97.5th percentile (one-sided); significant dimensions counted contiguously from the first component.

Decoding: OLS from GRU hidden state to target, grouped cross-validation on held-out episodes, mean-baseline-normalized held-out R^2. Circular targets decoded via parallel cos/sin models averaged. (NOT ridge alpha=0.01 - that was a summarizer error.)
PSD: short-time spectrogram, 20-timestep windows, 10-timestep overlap, averaged across units/windows/frequencies to one wideband power value per agent-episode
Unit subsampling for D_eff: fractions {0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}, n = 30 draws per fraction
Theil index T = (1/N) sum_i (x_i/mu) ln(x_i/mu); win ratio = n_given/(n_given + n_received)

Statistics: Dunnett one-vs-control for ablations; two-sided Mann-Whitney (unpaired); Wilcoxon signed-rank (paired); alpha = 0.05; NO multiple-comparison correction ('panel-level exploratory summaries')
Calibration identity (Supp .21.2): required source dipole moment p = E_max * pi * eps0 * x^6 / (R^3 * chi); dipole moment for target field p = 2*pi*eps0*x^3*E_max

Self-vs-induced field ratio (Supp .21.3): E_self/E_ind = x_obj^3 * |x_obj - r|^3 / (2*chi*R^3*r^3); approx x_obj^6/(2*chi*R^3*r^3) when r << x_obj; ~1e6 for x_obj = 5 cm, R = 0.25 cm, |chi| = 0.5, r = 1 cm
Self-vs-cons EOD ratio (Supp .21.4): E_self-EOD/E_cons-EOD = |x_cons - r|^3/r^3 = 9^3 = 729 for x_cons = 10 cm, r = 1 cm
METABOLIC COST OF EOD: entirely absent. No energy term in reward, no energetics citation in the bibliography (no Salazar & Stoddard, no Markham, no Lewis).

PREDATION: absent from the body text. Stoddard, Tran & Krahe (2019) on predation/crypsis is ref 64, cited ONCE in the supplementary Related Work, and miscited under 'EOD patterns carry information about identity, dominance, and aggression'. v1 listed predators as future work; v2 dropped them from Limitations entirely.

EVOLUTION: absent. 'Fitness' means only the RL reward ('individual fitness incentives'). v1's abstract said 'evolution-inspired rewards for individual fitness'; v2 removed that framing. No selection, heritability, or population dynamics.
Only cost mention is receiver-side: 'individuals can exploit conspecific signals as public information at low cost' (producer-scrounger, ref 47 Giraldeau & Caraco)

v1-only content dropped from v2: explicit 'freeloading' claim (agents reduce EOD rates while exploiting neighbors' active sensing), competitive/zero-sum vs non-competitive food framing, social EOD motifs defined as two agents within 15 cm for >= 4 timesteps, ~0.36 s displacement window

Negative result: agents show only size-dependent EOD rate REDUCTION, not the full EOD cessation displayed by real subordinate mormyrids (refs 43, 12). Authors flag testing under 'stronger social pressure' as future work.

Stated limitations: circular particles not elongated 3D bodies; no fluid dynamics; electrostatic assumption ignoring within-step electrodynamics at 12 ms; no multimodal (visual/mechanosensory) integration; no sexual dimorphism; brittle OOD generalization; no new experimental data collected

gaps_or_risks: CENTRAL GAP - the EOD-muting intervention is confounded and the paper never acknowledges it. Because the Mormyromast self-image is by construction the distortion of the agent's OWN EOD, clamping the EOD action to zero simultaneously destroys (i) the muted agent's private active electrolocation and (ii) its public social signal to conspecifics. The reported effects (reduced group food, increased nearest-neighbor distance) therefore cannot be attributed to loss of communication rather than loss of self-generated active sensing. No counterfactual/channel-isolating manipulation is run. Note: an early WebFetch summary claimed the paper says muting 'isolated the consequences of losing outgoing communication independent of impaired sensing' - that phrase does NOT appear in the paper (verified with grep); it was a summarizer hallucination. Do not cite it.

The operational definition of communication is purely effect-based ('EOD signals that are sensed by conspecifics via Knollenorgans and that influence their behavior'). It contains no sender-benefit criterion and therefore cannot distinguish a SIGNAL (maintained because it influences receivers) from a CUE (incidental information leakage that receivers eavesdrop on). This is the cue/signal distinction from animal-communication theory, and the paper's framework structurally cannot address it.

EOD emission is FREE. There is no energetic, metabolic, or predation-risk cost term anywhere in the reward (r_effort penalizes only movement/turn magnitude). With zero cost on emission there is no selective pressure that could trade off the private sensing benefit against the public signalling cost, so the model cannot in principle determine why EODs are emitted at the rates they are. This is the single largest lever available to a follow-up paper.

No evolutionary or selection dynamics of any kind. 'Fitness' in the paper means only the RL reward function. There is no population, no heritability, no selection over an emission-cost/benefit parameter space, hence no phase diagram over regimes where signalling is vs is not favoured. v1's abstract used the phrase 'evolution-inspired rewards' but v2 deliberately removed it.

Predation is absent from the body text. Stoddard, Tran & Krahe (2019) on predation and crypsis in the evolution of electric signalling is in the bibliography (ref 64) but is cited exactly once, in the supplementary Related Work, and is MISCITED - grouped with references about identity/dominance/aggression rather than about predation-driven signal cost. v1 named predators as future work; v2 dropped them from the Limitations section altogether.

No noise model whatsoever - no receptor noise, no sensory noise, no EOD timing jitter, no channel noise. Detection thresholds are hard clips on a deterministic field computation. This makes all 'detection range' claims deterministic geometry rather than signal-detection statements, and removes any notion of SNR, which is central to real electrosensory ecology.

Reward coefficient NUMERIC VALUES are never published. Methods 5.6 explicitly forward-references Supplementary .15.3 for 'reward coefficient values', but .15.3 gives only the symbols c_f and c_p and prose descriptions. Exact reproduction of the reward function is impossible from the paper; the GitHub repo (KempnerInstitute/wef) would be required.

RL hyperparameters are not reported. No learning rate, batch/minibatch size, discount factor gamma, number of PPO epochs, number of parallel envs, entropy coefficient, or BPTT horizon. The paper states only that hyperparameters were taken unchanged from the MAPPO codebase (Yu et al. 2022) with no tuning - which is itself a risk, since those defaults were tuned for MuJoCo-style continuous control, not this environment.
Episode length (in timesteps or seconds) is never stated anywhere in the paper or supplement, despite being needed to interpret every 'food eaten per episode' number.

Internal architecture inconsistency: Methods 5.6 describes tanh nonlinearities throughout with separate 256-unit action and value heads and 'no batch normalization or other regularization'; Supplementary .15.4 describes ReLU + LayerNorm MLP encoders with linear heads. These cannot both be true. Resolve against the repo before reimplementing.

Results are almost entirely qualitative/directional. Essentially no effect sizes, confidence intervals, or exact p-values appear in the text - only star annotations and mean +/- SEM in figures. The only hard numbers in the whole Results are D_eff = 81.3, 304 PCs for 90% variance, biting peak at ~40% of bout duration, and ~50% biting rate for confronting bouts. Even the IDI power-law exponents - arguably the headline biological validation - are withheld, with the admission that agent and real-fish exponents 'do not quantitatively match'.

No multiple-comparison correction is applied anywhere; the authors explicitly label all comparisons 'panel-level exploratory summaries'. Combined with n=30 episodes for most four-agent assays, individual intervention effects should be treated as suggestive only.

All post-training analyses come from a SINGLE selected seed (S1) out of 20, chosen by an ethological criterion that explicitly includes the size-food relationship. The authors themselves concede this makes Fig. 3M 'a quantitative confirmation, not an independent finding.' Any claim about the selected policy risks being a property of one seed rather than of the training setup; the paper offers only Fig. 12 as informal cross-seed reassurance.

Sensor ablations are applied at evaluation time with a frozen policy (no retraining). This measures how a policy trained WITH a channel degrades when the channel is removed, not what a fish adapted to lacking that channel would do. Ablation magnitudes therefore confound the causal contribution of the channel with out-of-distribution input shock.

Knollenorgan ablation zeroes the input channels, which is not the same as the biological manipulation the paper proposes as a testable prediction ('selectively blocking Knollenorgan-mediated signalling in real fish'). Zeroing a log-normalized signed channel places it at a value the network never saw during training, rather than at a plausible 'no conspecific detected' value.

Physics simplifications that could matter for any signalling analysis: strictly electrostatic within a 12 ms step (no waveform, no EOD shape, no frequency content - so 'waveform intensity carries size/sex information' is implemented as a hand-injected scalar metadata channel, not as anything the physics produces); first-order wall images only; 2D circular particles with radially symmetric receptor normals; no fluid dynamics; no multimodal integration; no sexual dimorphism.

Knollenorgans in the model encode ONLY the sign of the local field plus an externally supplied conspecific-size scalar. The size information is therefore injected by the experimenter, not sensed. Any claim that agents 'read conspecific size from EODs' is true by construction of the observation vector, not an emergent electrosensory result.

The bot-control result (patch-reach rate peaks at INTERMEDIATE bot EOD rate) is the paper's cleanest evidence that conspecific EODs act as usable social information, since the bot has no adaptive behaviour. But the non-monotonicity is never explained or quantified, and the bot's emission timing is explicitly noted to differ in temporal structure from trained agents - so it is not a clean substitute.

v1 vs v2 divergence is a citation hazard. v1 makes a prominent 'freeloading' claim (agents reduce their own EOD rate while exploiting neighbours' active sensing) with supporting motif analysis; v2 removes the freeloading framing entirely. If a follow-up paper wants to engage with or refute 'freeloading', it must cite v1 specifically - the claim is not in v2.

Acknowledged by the authors: no new experimental data were collected; agents do not reproduce the full EOD cessation seen in real subordinate mormyrids (only a graded size-dependent rate reduction); OOD generalization of MARL policies is brittle.
